title: Trump Says Washington Is in Denuclearisation Talks With Russia and China After New START's Lapse, as Wang Yi Tells Israel to Reverse West Bank Settlements
subhead: Trump confirmed on Newsmax that the US is negotiating nuclear disarmament with Moscow and Beijing weeks after the last US-Russia arms treaty expired, while China's foreign minister used a summit in Baku to call the Palestinian question 'the greatest historical injustice of this century' and demand Israel stop expanding settlements.

sections.heading: Washington Opens Denuclearisation Talks With Moscow and Beijing
sections.body:
President Trump said on Thursday, in an interview with Newsmax, that the United States is in talks with both Russia and China about nuclear disarmament. 'We're actually talking to Russia about that, and we're talking to China about that denuclearisation,' he said, adding that he would 'love to denuclearise if possible.' Newsmax reported that Trump discussed the subject with President Xi Jinping, though no details of either track were disclosed, according to Al Jazeera.

The remarks came shortly after the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty - the last major US-Russia arms control agreement - expired. Al Jazeera reports that Russia and the US together hold an estimated 86 percent of the world's nuclear weapons, each with more than 4,000 warheads, while China's arsenal has grown to about 620 warheads, per SIPRI. Trump claimed China will 'catch up' within five years.

A month after the treaty lapsed, French President Emmanuel Macron announced a Forward Deterrence Initiative in response to Russian nuclear signalling over Ukraine. Former Australian foreign minister Gareth Evans told Al Jazeera the world has 'become alarmingly complacent about the risks of nuclear war with every major nuclear arms control agreement dead, dying or on life support.'
sections.whyItMatters: With New START gone, there is now no treaty cap on the two largest arsenals. Trump's claim of trilateral talks is unverified and likely aspirational - China has repeatedly refused to join a US-Russia framework - but the statement itself is a signal that arms control has moved from a structured treaty regime to ad hoc leader-level diplomacy. If the talks are real, they are the only remaining channel constraining the three biggest nuclear powers.

sections.heading: China's Top Diplomat Demands Israel Reverse West Bank Settlements
sections.body:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog, during a meeting in Azerbaijan, that Israel should stop and reverse its 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements, China's foreign ministry said in a statement on Friday, according to Al Jazeera. Wang called the Palestinian question 'the greatest historical injustice of this century' and said the two-state solution is the only path forward.

Wang was in Baku as Xi Jinping's special representative to the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia, Xinhua reported. He also said the immediate priority is to fully open access to Gaza so a humanitarian 'catastrophe' does not spread. The intervention follows Xi's first visit to Egypt in a decade in September, where he called on Middle East states to reshape the region's security order and resist external influence.

China is Iran's largest trading partner, buying up to 90 percent of its oil according to the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, and holds a 25-year strategic partnership with Tehran signed in 2021, while also cultivating ties with Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE.
sections.whyItMatters: Beijing is translating its economic weight in the Gulf into explicit political positions on the Israeli-Palestinian file, a domain Washington has long owned. Directly pressing an Israeli president to reverse settlements - language rarely used even by European capitals - marks China positioning itself as an alternative diplomatic broker in the Middle East while the US is consumed by the Iran war.

sections.heading: EU Closes Ranks Behind Kyiv as Zelensky Requests $79 Billion
sections.body:
European Union leaders urged continued support for Ukraine on Friday, the second day of a Brussels summit attended by President Volodymyr Zelensky, amid a deepening rift with Washington. European Council President Antonio Costa said: 'This is no time to withdraw support to Ukraine... Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure,' per Al Jazeera.

Zelensky asked EU leaders for an additional 70 billion euros ($79 billion) next year, saying the war will cost 155 billion euros in 2026. He called EU leaders 'real leaders,' an apparent dig at Trump, who last weekend unilaterally announced an 'energy ceasefire' that Ukraine abandoned on Thursday after Russia kept striking Ukrainian power infrastructure. Trump called the resumed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries 'a disgrace,' while Zelensky told Piers Morgan he felt betrayed and told the Financial Times that the US diesel deal with Moscow 'will put more money straight into Putin's pocket.'

Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal told Reuters the EU will likely need a new loan for Ukraine's budget gap, warning 'this winter will be once again like hell.' Austria's Chancellor Christian Stocker urged caution on the figures. Al Jazeera reported some European officials are privately asking Zelensky to tone down his public criticism of Trump.
sections.whyItMatters: The transatlantic split is now operational, not rhetorical: Washington is cutting intelligence support and easing sanctions on Russian oil while Europe scrambles to backfill. Kyiv's $79bn ask - and Europe's hesitation over how to fund it - will determine whether Ukraine can hold its energy grid and front line through the winter without US backing.

sections.heading: G20 Finance Chiefs Meet in Bangkok Under the Shadow of the Iran War
sections.body:
G20 finance ministers and central bank governors gathered in Bangkok alongside the IMF and World Bank annual meetings, with the economic fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran set to dominate, Al Jazeera reported. Disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping has kept crude oil above $100 a barrel for much of the past eight months, straining Gulf and Asian budgets.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was a notable absence, with Washington citing 'domestic engagements' and sending deputy and undersecretary-level officials instead. Australia's Treasurer Jim Chalmers said he would call for an end to the Middle East conflicts and the reopening of Hormuz 'because that's what the global economy desperately needs.' The Bangkok meeting will shape the agenda for the G20 leaders' summit in Miami on December 14-15.

Separately, Iraq devalued its dinar to ease a cash crunch, leaving traders facing rising import costs, while a Reuters report noted a data point underscoring the war's second-order effects on Iran's civilian economy.
sections.whyItMatters: The Iran war has become a global macro problem: sustained triple-digit oil is feeding inflation and rate pressure well beyond the Gulf. The absence of the US Treasury secretary from the chair's own meeting and the pushback from allies like Australia signal that Washington's war is being treated by partners as a shared economic liability they want wound down.

sections.heading: Gaza Malnutrition Reaches 'Catastrophic' Levels as Israel Halts Commercial Goods
sections.body:
Malnutrition and starvation rates in Gaza have reached 'catastrophic' levels, the Palestinian Ministry of Health said on Friday, marking World Food Day. At least 466 Palestinians have died of malnutrition and starvation since 2024, with children accounting for one-third of deaths, Al Jazeera reported. The ministry projects 74,200 children will need acute malnutrition treatment through April 2027, and warns more than 1.4 million people - 67 percent of Gaza's population - will face crisis-level food insecurity or worse through the end of 2026.

The figures land as Israeli authorities said no commercial goods have entered Gaza for days, with COGAT citing a claimed tax dispute between merchants and Hamas. Gaza's private truckers union head Nahed Sheheiber denied the Israeli account. The halt cuts off perishable foods and winter clothing ahead of colder months. UNICEF said gains against hunger are fragile and urged that crossings stay open, with spokesperson Ricardo Pires warning 'we can't go back to a situation where children and families are not getting all the supplies, goods, and services that they require.'
sections.whyItMatters: The ceasefire that was meant to let aid in is not preventing famine-level outcomes, and the commercial-supply halt removes the market component that keeps prices in check. With winter approaching and aid groups unable to meet needs alone, the humanitarian trajectory is worsening even under a nominal truce.

sections.heading: Ethiopia Installs Interim Government in Tigray After Crushing the Uprising
sections.body:
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced on Friday that an interim administration will run Tigray for six months, with free elections to follow, after federal forces retook the northern region, Al Jazeera reported. The government appointed five officials, including the mayor of the capital Mekelle, who will carry out directives issued directly from the federal government.

The move follows the defeat of a September offensive by the Tigray People's Liberation Front and allied armed groups aimed at toppling Abiy. TPLF fighters surrendered in Mekelle in early October, and Eritrean troops who had entered Tigray withdrew after heavy Ethiopian drone strikes. Ethiopia and Eritrea have accused each other of inciting war, with the US urging de-escalation in a call between Abiy and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

The TPLF has not yet responded to the interim-government announcement. The region is still scarred by the 2020-2022 war, which killed almost 600,000 people and left key peace-deal commitments - the return of displaced people and TPLF disarmament - unmet.
sections.whyItMatters: A federally appointed administration with direct orders from Addis Ababa effectively ends Tigray's autonomy and could reignite the grievances behind the war that killed hundreds of thousands. Combined with the unresolved Ethiopia-Eritrea standoff, the Horn remains a live conflict zone where a wider regional war could still break out.

bottomLine: The day's most consequential shift was in the nuclear domain: with New START expired, Trump said Washington is now in denuclearisation talks with both Russia and China - an unverified claim that nonetheless reflects a world where the last treaty cap on the largest arsenals is gone and discipline rests on leader-level diplomacy alone. China pressed further into Middle East politics as Wang Yi demanded Israel reverse West Bank settlements and called the Palestinian question the century's greatest injustice, while the EU closed ranks behind Zelensky's $79bn request amid a widening breach with Washington. Downstream, the Iran war kept oil above $100 and dominated the G20 finance talks in Bangkok, and in Gaza malnutrition reached what the health ministry calls catastrophic levels even under a ceasefire that is not stopping the slide.
